papers.titleEn: Robust Dipicolinic Acid-Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Wide-Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The anchoring group of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) hole‐transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material, denoted by XS21 , engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual‐action mechanism of pyridine–Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate‐metal interaction. Furthermore, XS21 imparts both low acid‐dissociation constants ( K a ) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide‐bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing XS21 deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open‐circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating XS21 into monolithic all‐perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi‐dentate pyridine‐carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next‐generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.
papers.filename: Bo Xu, Adv. Mater., 2026, Robust Dipicolinic Acid-Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Wide-Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics

papers.titleEn: Deep Learning-Enabled Plasmonic-Catalytic Au@PBA Array for Simultaneous SERS/Colorimetric Quantification of Exhaled Benzene-Related VOCs
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate determination of benzene-related volatile organic compounds (B-VOCs) in exhaled breath is of considerable importance for disease screening and occupational exposure assessment. However, the simultaneous identification and quantification of structurally similar B-VOCs remain a challenge due to severe cross-interference and nonlinear signal coupling in multicomponent matrices. Herein, we report a deep learning-enabled plasmonic-catalytic sensor array based on core−shell Au@PBA(M) (M = Co, Ni, Mn) nanozymes featuring an ultrathin PBA shell for the multiplexed analysis of five B-VOCs (toluene, ethylbenzene, xylene, styrene, and phenol). The dual-response core−shell Au@PBA nanoparticles provide both strong plasmonic enhancement and peroxidase-mimicking activity, enabling the catalytic oxidation of TMB with concurrent surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) and colorimetric readouts. In the presence of different B-VOCs, the oxidation process is inhibited to different extents due to the differential binding affinities of the B-VOCs to the Au@PBA nanoparticles, generating highly characteristic dual-mode fingerprints. Based on this mechanism, linear discriminant analysis enabled reliable discrimination of the five B-VOCs. Notably, quantitative analysis of single-component systems demonstrated broad quantitative ranges of 0.001−500 ppm for ethylbenzene and phenol and 0.005−500 ppm for toluene, xylene, and styrene. More importantly, the integration of multichannel SERS fingerprints with an artificial neural network enabled simultaneous quantification of five B-VOCs in 25 complex breath-relevant samples, yielding excellent predictive accuracy (R2 > 0.97) and low root-mean-square errors (0.27−0.30 in log10 scale). These results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively resolves the cross-responsiveness of complex gas mixtures, providing a robust and noninvasive platform for intelligent breath analysis and environmental monitoring.
papers.filename: Mei Li, Anal. Chem., 2026, Deep Learning-Enabled Plasmonic-Catalytic Au@PBA Array for Simultaneous SERS Colorimetric Quantification of Exhaled Benzene-Related VOCs

papers.titleEn: Programmable Nanozyme Gating: A Molecular Ejector Switch (MES) for High-Fidelity miRNA-21 Sensing
papers.abstract: Nucleotide-level variants in miRNA or pathogen genomes can critically reprogram gene-regulatory networks or enhance disease severity, highlighting the urgent need for sensing platforms capable of resolving subtle sequence discrepancies. In this article, we present a programmable molecular ejector switch (MES) that functions as a confinement-gating smart nanozyme for adaptive nucleic-acid sensing. By integrating the etb topology of mesoporous Co-IRMOF-74-II with single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gatekeepers, the MES transforms passive MOF scaffolds into an active logical device. Driven by the balance between van der Waals attraction and electrostatic repulsion, the ssDNA gatekeepers can be reversibly accommodated within the pores to block mass transport through the MES. Upon target binding, hybridization displaces the ssDNA gatekeeper, while the resulting rigid duplex is less compatible with pore re-entry, thereby restoring the overall nanozyme activity. As a proof of concept, the miRNA-21 sensor furnishes accurate colorimetric readouts (LOD: 0.84 nM; log-linear range 1-300 nM), while concurrent fluorescent signals (LOD: 0.10 nM; linear range 0.2-50 nM) cross-validate the gating logic. The sensor outputs exhibit a monotonic dependence on the mismatch degree, enabling high-fidelity discrimination of multi-nucleotide variants. This modular confinement-gating strategy is readily adaptable to other nucleic acid biomarkers, offering a versatile scaffold for the development of intelligent diagnostic devices.
papers.filename: Dan Shan, ACS Sens., 2026, Programmable Nanozyme Gating A Molecular Ejector Switch (MES) for High-Fidelity miRNA-21 Sensing
